alignments.definition: Repeated institutional and market behavior that connects changing work/skill requirements to demand forecasting, training, assessment and targeted employment matching rather than treating training and placement as isolated stages.
alignments.boundary: Does not prove a private project-work marketplace, employer willingness to pay an orchestrator, high-quality gig economics, training causality, or that trained capability is currently spare/callable.
counterexamples: Training and employment services remain disconnected and placement does not become more targeted despite repeated programs.
Observed matching mechanisms are administrative only and employers continue to recruit without using the linked training/assessment channels.
AI-driven skill change reduces demand for the trained capabilities faster than matching infrastructure can adapt.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Four reviewed observations across national, Jiangsu and Xuzhou levels and multiple dates independently describe a linked training-to-work matching behavior. This satisfies diversity gates only for ontology promotion review, not for a business or transaction route.

alignments.definition: Repeated platform/regulatory behavior that makes digital commerce more governable through identity and qualification checks, rule transparency, after-sales handling, dispute resolution, consumer protection and merchant-service matching.
alignments.boundary: Does not prove merchants experience a monetizable pain, that regulation improves merchant margins, that users will pay a new intermediary, or that a government/local platform model transfers to commercial platforms.
counterexamples: Governance requirements increase compliance cost without improving trust, dispute outcomes or merchant operating stability.
Merchants and consumers bypass formal trust mechanisms because incumbent platform processes are already sufficient.
Local adoption metrics fade after launch and do not persist without public promotion.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Four independent reviewed observations across research, national regulation, provincial guidance and local operation coherently describe a trust/governance infrastructure layer. Readiness is ontology governance only; merchant pain and willingness-to-pay remain unproved.

alignments.definition: Behavior that formalizes reuse and replacement circulation through recycling networks, second-hand trading, appraisal/inspection, remanufacturing and trade-in channels.
alignments.boundary: Does not treat subsidized replacement as organic recommerce demand, does not prove resale of collected goods, and does not establish profitable reuse economics or resource ownership/availability.
counterexamples: Trade-in activity falls sharply when fiscal/platform subsidies are removed.
Collected goods are scrapped without meaningful second-hand or remanufacturing circulation.
Inspection and quality-trust mechanisms remain too weak for repeated secondary transactions.
alignments.alignment_rationale: National, provincial and local observations point in the same circulation/formalization direction, while explicit local evidence also shows substantial subsidy contamination. Three observations remain below the default promotion-review count gate.

alignments.definition: Behavioral expansion and formalization of paid pet services across medical, boarding, grooming, training, insurance, travel and pet-friendly consumption contexts.
alignments.boundary: Does not infer that every pet-service subcategory is growing, that national survey usage transfers to Xuzhou, that local service presence proves provider quality, or that pet spending creates an orchestration opportunity.
counterexamples: Pet-service usage or category share declines despite overall pet-market growth.
Formalization policy is not followed by durable provider/service adoption.
Local service density grows but repeat paid usage and service quality remain weak.
alignments.alignment_rationale: National usage, Jiangsu formalization action and Xuzhou service-ecosystem evidence are directionally coherent but only three reviewed observations support the grouping; medical share decline is retained as counterevidence against blanket pet-service growth.

alignments.definition: Behavior that reallocates or pools logistics/warehouse capacity through third-party logistics, digital capacity-demand matching, unified/shared warehousing and integrated fulfillment systems.
alignments.boundary: Does not infer that market vacancy is callable spare capacity, that shared warehousing is profitable, that tenants surrender routing control, or that one local cloud-warehouse case generalizes to the national market.
counterexamples: Warehouse absorption recovers because dedicated occupiers expand while shared/third-party orchestration does not gain durable share.
Digital matching platforms fail to reduce empty running, idle space or empty loads in measured operations.
Shared warehouse adoption requires subsidies or founder-heavy bespoke operations and does not repeat across industries.
alignments.alignment_rationale: Three observations span market leasing behavior, national capacity-matching policy and a local shared-fulfillment operation. They suggest a coherent orchestration mechanism but remain below the four-observation promotion-review gate and do not prove callable idle capacity.
